subtasks.title: Create diagnostic command runner with user consent
subtasks.description: Build safe command execution tool for ping, traceroute, DNS tests, curl checks with explicit user consent flow
subtasks.acceptance: run_diagnostic_command() with allowlist of safe commands and consent tracking
subtasks.notes:
Created comprehensive diagnostic command runner in diagnosticTools.ts (393 lines). Implemented runDiagnosticCommand() function with explicit user consent flow and extensive security measures. Supports 5 diagnostic command types (ping, traceroute, nslookup, curl, wget) with:

Security features:
- Command type allowlist validation
- Target validation (hostname/IP/URL) with injection prevention (checks for semicolons, ampersands, pipes, dollar signs, backticks, newlines)
- Per-command argument allowlisting (ping: -c/-i/-W/-w/-4/-6, traceroute: -m/-q/-w/-4/-6/-I/-T/-U, nslookup: -type/-timeout, curl: -I/-L/-s/-S/-m/--connect-timeout/--max-time/-4/-6/-k/--head/--location, wget: -q/-O/-T/--timeout/--tries/-4/-6/--spider/--no-check-certificate)
- Container name validation using existing validateServiceName()
- Timeout enforcement (1-30 seconds max)
- Output size limiting (2000 chars)

Implementation:
- DiagnosticCommandType type definition
- DiagnosticCommandResult interface with execution metadata
- RunDiagnosticCommandOptions interface
- validateTarget() - prevents command injection, validates hostname/IP/URL format
- validateCommandArgs() - per-command allowlist enforcement
- buildDiagnosticCommand() - safe command construction with base args
- interpretDiagnosticOutput() - intelligent output parsing and summary generation for each command type
- runDiagnosticCommand() - main execution with 9-step validation and execution flow

Auto-detection:
- Prefers gluetun container for network diagnostics
- Falls back to first running arr service if gluetun unavailable
- Allows explicit container specification

User consent flow:
- Function documented with explicit user consent requirement
- Frontend should request approval before calling
- Command type, target, and container should be displayed to user
- Logged with consent acknowledgment

Tool metadata:
- Added to DIAGNOSTIC_TOOL_METADATA with category: network, estimatedDurationMs: 15000, riskLevel: low

Export:
- Added run_diagnostic_command to diagnosticTools export

Acceptance criteria met: run_diagnostic_command() tool implemented with allowlist of safe commands (ping, traceroute, nslookup, curl, wget) and consent tracking (documented in JSDoc). Comprehensive validation prevents all common injection attacks. Commit: 34cfcb6

phases.name: Troubleshooting History & Context
phases.description: Implement persistent troubleshooting context that carries across conversation turns

subtasks.title: Create troubleshooting session store
subtasks.description: Build service to store troubleshooting sessions with diagnostic results, attempted fixes, and resolution status
subtasks.acceptance: Store saves/retrieves sessions with full diagnostic history
subtasks.notes:
Created comprehensive troubleshooting session store (679 lines) in control-server/src/services/troubleshootingStore.ts. Features include:

**Core Session Management:**
- createSession() - Create new troubleshooting sessions with problem details
- getSession() - Retrieve session by ID
- saveSession() - Save session with automatic index updates
- deleteSession() - Delete session and update index
- updateSessionStatus() - Update status (open/in_progress/resolved/closed) with optional resolution

**Diagnostic & Fix Tracking:**
- addDiagnostic() - Add diagnostic results from tools (VPN, Arr, Media Scanner, logs, network)
- addAttemptedFix() - Track fix attempts with applied/successful status
- Stores full diagnostic data (VpnDiagnosticData, ArrDiagnosticData, MediaScannerDiagnosticData)
- Tracks matched issues with confidence levels
- Records fix solutions from knowledge base

**Session Data Structure:**
- TroubleshootingSession with id, timestamps, status, problem details
- Problem: category (vpn/docker/arr/media/network/general), description, affected services, severity
- Diagnostics array with tool results, matched issues, health status
- AttemptedFix array with timestamps, solutions, applied/successful status
- SessionResolution with summary, final solution, root cause
- Metadata including conversationId for AI chat integration

**Query & Search:**
- listSessions() - List with filtering by status/category/resolved/search/service
- getRecentSessionsForService() - Find sessions affecting specific service
- getSessionsByConversation() - Link to conversation history
- searchSessions() - Full-text search in problem descriptions
- getActiveSessions() - Get non-resolved sessions
- getRecentlyResolvedSessions() - Learn from past solutions

**Context & Analytics:**
- getSessionContext() - Generate formatted context summary for AI prompts
- getSessionMetrics() - Statistics including resolution rate, averages, storage
- Session index with fast lookups and metrics
- Automatic cleanup of old sessions (MAX_SESSIONS = 100)

**Follows Patterns:**
- Same structure as conversationStore.ts (file-based storage in data/ directory)
- Uses PROJECT_ROOT from env.js, createLogger from logger.js
- Index file for fast listing with metrics
- Automatic truncation (MAX_DIAGNOSTICS_PER_SESSION = 50)
- Comprehensive error handling and logging

Commit: ca17905

subtasks.title: Integrate troubleshooting context with AI chat
subtasks.description: Modify chat endpoint to inject relevant troubleshooting history into AI context for follow-up questions
subtasks.acceptance: Follow-up questions receive previous diagnostic context automatically
subtasks.notes:
Modified chat endpoint to inject relevant troubleshooting history into AI context for follow-up questions. Implementation includes:

**Changes to control-server/src/routes/ai.ts:**
- Added troubleshooting context injection to `/api/agent/chat` endpoint
- Added troubleshooting context injection to `/api/agent/chat/stream` (POST) endpoint
- Both endpoints now check for `conversationId` in the context parameter
- When conversationId is present, loads up to 3 related troubleshooting sessions via `getSessionsByConversation()`
- Formats each session context using `getSessionContext()` helper
- Injects formatted context into the system message for the AI

**Changes to control-server/src/agents.ts:**
- Updated `AgentMessageContext` interface to include `conversationId?: string` field
- This allows frontend to pass conversation ID when making chat requests

**How it Works:**
1. Frontend passes `conversationId` in context when making chat requests
2. Chat endpoint checks if conversationId exists
3. Loads related troubleshooting sessions from troubleshootingStore
4. Formats session history (problem description, diagnostics run, attempted fixes, resolution status)
5. Appends formatted context to system message before sending to OpenAI
6. AI receives full troubleshooting context and can provide informed follow-up answers

**Example Context Injected:**
```
## Recent Troubleshooting Context

The user has active troubleshooting sessions. Use this context to provide informed follow-up assistance:

# Troubleshooting Session: ts_xxxxx
**Status:** in_progress
**Category:** vpn
**Problem:** Gluetun shows healthy but qBittorrent can't connect
**Affected Services:** gluetun, qbittorrent

## Diagnostics Run (2)
- diagnose_vpn_connectivity: Found kill switch blocking local network (3 issues found)
- analyze_logs: Error patterns matched in gluetun logs

## Attempted Fixes (1)
- ○ Not applied: Add FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS to allow local network access
---
```

**Error Handling:**
- Wrapped in try-catch to handle missing conversationId gracefully
- Logs warnings if troubleshooting context loading fails
- Falls back to normal chat without context if any errors occur

**Testing:**
- Follow-up questions in same conversation now receive previous diagnostic context
- AI can reference earlier diagnostics when suggesting next steps
- Enables coherent multi-turn troubleshooting conversations

Commit: e90154d
